template.title: Covering design C({v},{k},{t})
template.statement: Find {k}-subsets (blocks) of {{1, ..., {v}}} such that every {t}-subset lies in some block, with as few blocks as possible.
template.submission: Text file: one block per line, {k} distinct points from 1..{v} separated by spaces.

lotto.title: Covering design C({v},{k},{t},{m})
lotto.statement: Find {k}-subsets (blocks) of {{1, ..., {v}}} such that every {m}-subset meets some block in at least {t} points, with as few blocks as possible.

score: the number of blocks (smaller is better)
best_text: The best known size in the Covering Repository is {best} blocks ({holder}); a design with fewer blocks improves it.
bound_source: the larger of Schönheim's bound and the La Jolla Covering Repository's listed lower bound (m = t); for m > t the counting bound C(v,m) / (the m-subsets one block meets in at least t points) and, for t = 2, Turán's theorem (the pairs inside blocks form a graph with no independent m-set: at least C(v,2) - t(v,m-1) edges, C(k,2) per block); the method is named after the value
holder_unknown: not named in the site's export; see the entry on coveringrepository.com
holder_sources: our own records (quantavane-covering-records); the site's list of recent uploads and derived coverings, read with each daily export since 1 Nov 2026; for entries unchanged since then, the credit in the La Jolla Covering Repository's final data (frozen 1 March 2026)
open_rule: every entry whose best known size is above the lower bound named in the cell; entries that equal it are solved and left out. A cell may still be optimal by a sharper bound than these.
left_out: 16566 entries equal to their lower bound (solved); 5155 entries with m > t and at most 3 blocks (a short case analysis settles them); 14439 entries whose check would be very long: t = m with more than 10^8 t-subsets to mark (blocks x C(k,t)), or m > t with more than 1,000 blocks
